sections.label: Home Team Corps Bill enactment
sections.summary: The HTC Bill will regularise NCDCC's statutory status and create a single HTC Council overseeing NCDCC and NPCC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The enactment of the Home Team Corps (HTC) Bill will regularise the statutory status of NCDCC and create a single HTC Council comprising representatives of senior officials from SPF, Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) and MOE to oversee both NCDCC and NPCC.

sections.label: HTC Bill and NPCC Act repeal
sections.summary: Enacting the HTC Bill and repealing the NPCC Act will formalise administration of NCDCC and NPCC, providing better youth support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: With the enactment of the HTC Bill and the repeal of the NPCC Act, the administration of NCDCC and NPCC will be formalised, providing better support to our youth.

sections.label: Application approval and appeal process
sections.summary: The passage asks the Senior Minister of State under what circumstances applications will be approved and whether there will be an appeal process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State share under what circumstances will these applications be approved and whether there will be an appeal process?

sections.label: Schools offering NPCC and NCDCC
sections.summary: Currently 142 Secondary schools offer NPCC, and a smaller number of schools offer NCDCC as CCAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Currently, there are 142 Secondary schools offering NPCC, and a smaller number of schools offering NCDCC as CCAs.

sections.label: NPCC and NCDCC at Primary level
sections.summary: Only Secondary school students currently benefit from NPCC or NCDCC, and the Ministry is asked to consider offering them at Primary level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At present, only Secondary school students are able to reap the benefits of participating in NPCC or NCDCC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would like the Ministry to consider setting up NPCC and NCDCC as CCAs at the Primary school level, too.

sections.label: Recruitment initiatives for NPCC and NCDCC
sections.summary: MOE is urged to work with SPF and SCDF on potential recruitment initiatives for NPCC and NCDCC cadets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: On that note, I would like to urge MOE to work with SPF and SCDF on potential recruitment initiatives for NPCC and NCDCC cadets.

sections.label: NPCC and NCDCC single entity
sections.summary: The NPCC and NCDCC should come under a single Home Team Corps entity, retaining identity while streamlining resources and training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From a resourcing and development perspective, it makes sense for the NPCC and NCDCC to come under a single entity − the Home Team Corps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This will allow each unit to retain its own identity, at the same time, streamline resources and training curriculum to enhance synergy.

sections.label: MOE and Home Team partnership
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOE will partner with the Home Team to plan a more integrated training structure and curriculum for NPCC and NCDCC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this regard, I hope that MOE will partner with the Home Team to plan for a more integrated and inter-related training structure and curriculum for both NPCC and NCDCC.

sections.label: Tracking officers and engaging cadets
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Home Team tracks officers who were NPCC or NCDCC cadets and has strategies to engage cadets beyond CCA training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In line with this suggestion, I would also like to enquire if the Home Team currently tracks the number of its officers who were from NPCC or NCDCC and whether they have any existing strategies to engage the cadets beyond their CCA training.

sections.label: PR and non-citizen cadet enrolment
sections.summary: PRs and non-citizens meeting selection criteria are enrolled as cadets, about 11% of NPCC and NCDCC cadets, with 8% to 9% of the cohort enrolling annually.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The PRs and non-citizens who meet the selection criteria have been enrolled as cadets, and about 11% of our NPCC and NCDCC cadets are PRs and non-citizens.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For the spaces that are available, currently between 8% and 9% of the student cohort enrol within the NPCC and NCDCC annually.

sections.label: Home Team engagement and no preference
sections.summary: The Home Team invites officers to events and sends officers to engage cadets on careers, but gives no preferential treatment to NPCC and NCDCC applicants.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: They extend invitations to join officers in the Insight SPF and the Annual Workplan Seminar, send its Careers Centre Officers and Careers Counsellors to directly engage with the cadets to consider viable career options within the Home Team.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: However, there is no preferential treatment for applicants with NPCC and NCDCC background.
